opportunities.summary: **Context** `resolveLilySdkConfig` in `src/config/resolve-config.ts` calls `resolveCredential` unconditionally for `LILY_API_KEY` and `LILY_AUTH_TOKEN`. `resolveCredential` reads `process.env[envName]` with no `typeof process !== 'undefined'` guard, while `resolveBaseUrl` and `LilySdk.create()` in `src/sdk.ts` do guard. The SDK ships a browser build (`dist/browser/`, ES2022, no Node globals per `tsup.config.ts`), but any `new LilySdk({ baseUrl })` or `LilySdk.create({}) ` in a browser throws `ReferenceError: process is not defined` at config resolution, even when no credentials are involved. **Proposed Change** Guard the env access in `resolveCredential` (`typeof process === 'undefined' ? undefined : process.env[envName]`) so the resolved config is identical in browsers, and add a regression test that resolves config in an environment without a `process` global. **Acceptance Criteria** - `resolveLilySdkConfig({ baseUrl: 'https://api.example.com' })` succeeds with `process` deleted/undefined. - No `process` reference remains unguarded in `src/config/resolve-config.ts`. - A regression test simulates the browser environment and asserts both `new LilySdk(...)` and the config resolver w

opportunities.title: [Bounty: $60] Report the real HTTP status when a non-2xx error body fails to parse as JSON
opportunities.summary: **Context** In `createFetchHttpClient` (`src/http/fetch-http-client.ts`), `parseResponse` runs before the status check. When a server error (e.g. 500) declares `content-type: application/json` but returns an empty or malformed body, `response.json()` rejects and `parseResponse` throws `LilyValidationError` with code `RESPONSE_VALIDATION_ERROR` and status 500; the catch block then rethrows it as a `LilySdkError`. Callers see a confusing "Failed to parse response body as JSON" validation error instead of the actual server failure (`LilyServerError`/appropriate `LilyApiError`), and lose the status-aware handling they'd otherwise get. **Proposed Change** Decide JSON handling per status before throwing: keep the strict parse-and-throw `LilyValidationError` for successful (2xx) responses, but for non-ok responses treat an unparseable body as an API failure instead — throw a plain `LilyApiError` carrying the real status code with the raw content-type and the attempted-body text surfaced in `details`, rather than a body-parse validation error.
